verdict_text: NO. The sharding and index-file requirements (Required result 5: shard files, `model.safetensors.index.json` with a complete `weight_map`, the 256 MiB per-shard cap, oversized tensors alone in their own shard) are entirely delegated to `save_sharded_safetensors` from an external module `_ckpt` whose code is not part of the artifact, so the artifact cannot be shown to satisfy clause 5. Likewise, the input loading depends on `_ckpt.load_checkpoint`, so the "tensor names do not change" guarantee (clause 4) rests on unverified code. The visible logic is otherwise correct: the two regexes select exactly the 64 projection matrices and the 48 buffers, bfloat16 casting uses `.to(torch.bfloat16)` as required, everything else is upcast to float32, and all four required checks are asserted before writing. Under the condition's rule that the solution be a standalone script using only PyTorch and `safetensors`, the reliance on `_ckpt` also violates the artifact's own submission constraints.
